title: [27/7/2024] The proportion of qualified graduates
prompt: The two charts below show the proportion of qualified graduates in a particular country. To summarize information by selecting key characteristics and compiling a report and, if necessary, make a comparison.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the proportions of graduates with different levels of qualifications in Arts and Science fields in a particular country for two years, namely 1980 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, most qualification types experienced relatively modest changes, with Ph.D degree holders increasing notably in both fields, whereas first degree attainment declined across both disciplines. Additionally, Master and Ph.D of Science represented the largest proportion of graduates in both years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding postgraduate qualifications at the doctoral level, Ph.D Science accounted for a quarter of all degrees in 1980, significantly higher than Ph.D Art, which represented merely 2% of graduates. By 2008, Ph.D Science had risen to 30%, becoming the most common qualification. Similarly, Ph.D Art experienced dramatic growth, more than tripling to 7%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining qualification types, Master degrees in Science constituted 29% of total graduates in 1980, substantially exceeding Master Art degrees at 13%. The former remained unchanged at 29% in 2008, while the latter decreased slightly to 12%. Concerning first degrees, Science accounted for one-fifth of qualifications in 1980 compared to 11% for Art, but both categories experienced declines by 2008, falling to 12% and 10% respectively.
